savoy_cabbage.label: savoy_cabbage
savoy_cabbage.name: Savoy cabbage
savoy_cabbage.description: (Brassica oleracea var. sabauda L. or Brassica oleracea Savoy Cabbage Group) is a variety or cultivar group of the plant species Brassica oleracea. Savoy cabbage is a winter vegetable and one of several cabbage varieties. It has crinkled, emerald green leaves, which are crunchy with a slightly elastic consistency on the palate.

kale.label: kale
kale.name: Kale
kale.description: A leafy cultivar of Brassica oleracea with tightly curled, fibrous leaves. Popular in cold-climate gardens because frost improves its flavor.

artichoke.label: artichoke
artichoke.name: Artichoke
artichoke.description: The edible flower bud of a large thistle, harvested before it blooms. The fleshy base of each bract and the heart are the parts eaten.

rutabaga.label: rutabaga
rutabaga.name: Rutabaga
rutabaga.description: A root vegetable that arose as a natural cross between cabbage and turnip. Its dense, slightly sweet flesh is common in winter stews.

fennel.label: fennel
fennel.name: Fennel
fennel.description: A crisp, anise-flavored bulb vegetable whose feathery fronds and seeds are also used as an herb and spice. Native to the Mediterranean coast.

okra.label: okra
okra.name: Okra
okra.description: A warm-season pod vegetable known for the mucilaginous texture it releases when cut, which is prized as a natural thickener in stews.

parsnip.label: parsnip
parsnip.name: Parsnip
parsnip.description: A pale, carrot-shaped root vegetable that develops a nutty sweetness after exposure to frost, when stored starches convert to sugar.

radicchio.label: radicchio
radicchio.name: Radicchio
radicchio.description: A chicory grown for its dense, wine-red leaves and pleasantly bitter flavor. Often grilled to mellow the bitterness.

kohlrabi.label: kohlrabi
kohlrabi.name: Kohlrabi
kohlrabi.description: A cabbage relative grown for its swollen, above-ground stem rather than its leaves. The pale bulb has a mild flavor similar to broccoli stalk.

jicama.label: jicama
jicama.name: Jicama
jicama.description: A crisp, sweet root vegetable from a climbing legume vine. Eaten raw, its watery crunch resembles a cross between an apple and a potato.

watercress.label: watercress
watercress.name: Watercress
watercress.description: A fast-growing aquatic plant harvested for its peppery leaves. It roots directly in flowing streams and shallow ponds.

endive.label: endive
endive.name: Endive
endive.description: A slightly bitter salad green grown by forcing the roots to sprout in complete darkness, which keeps the compact leaves pale and tender.

taro.label: taro
taro.name: Taro
taro.description: A starchy tropical corm that must be cooked thoroughly, since the raw flesh contains calcium oxalate crystals that irritate the mouth.

chayote.label: chayote
chayote.name: Chayote
chayote.description: A pale green, single-seeded squash from a climbing vine, with a mild flavor that takes on whatever it is cooked with.

salsify.label: salsify
salsify.name: Salsify
salsify.description: A slender root vegetable sometimes called the oyster plant for the faint briny note some tasters detect when it is cooked.

sorrel.label: sorrel
sorrel.name: Sorrel
sorrel.description: A leafy green with a distinctly sour, lemony bite caused by naturally occurring oxalic acid in its leaves.

kiwano.label: kiwano
kiwano.name: Kiwano
kiwano.description: Also called horned melon, this African fruit has spiky orange skin and bright green, jelly-like flesh with a flavor between banana and cucumber.

persimmon.label: persimmon
persimmon.name: Persimmon
persimmon.description: An orange tree fruit that ranges from astringent until fully soft-ripe to naturally sweet, depending on the cultivar grown.

durian.label: durian
durian.name: Durian
durian.description: A large, thorn-covered Southeast Asian fruit famous for a smell strong enough to get it banned from many hotels and public transit.

lychee.label: lychee
lychee.name: Lychee
lychee.description: A small tropical fruit with a rough, rosy shell hiding pale, fragrant, and very juicy flesh around a single glossy seed.

starfruit.label: starfruit
starfruit.name: Starfruit
starfruit.description: A waxy yellow fruit that forms a perfect five-pointed star shape when sliced crosswise, used as a garnish as often as a snack.

quince.label: quince
quince.name: Quince
quince.description: A hard, aromatic fruit that is nearly inedible raw but turns a deep rose color and soft texture once slowly cooked.

mangosteen.label: mangosteen
mangosteen.name: Mangosteen
mangosteen.description: A thick, deep-purple rind encloses segmented white flesh often called the queen of tropical fruits for its delicate sweet-tart flavor.

jabuticaba.label: jabuticaba
jabuticaba.name: Jabuticaba
jabuticaba.description: A Brazilian tree fruit unusual for growing directly on the trunk and older branches rather than at the tips of twigs.

cherimoya.label: cherimoya
cherimoya.name: Cherimoya
cherimoya.description: A green, scaly-skinned fruit with creamy white flesh often compared to a blend of banana, pineapple, and strawberry.

longan.label: longan
longan.name: Longan
longan.description: A small brown-shelled fruit related to lychee, nicknamed dragon's eye because the black seed shows through the translucent flesh.

feijoa.label: feijoa
feijoa.name: Feijoa
feijoa.description: An egg-shaped green fruit with a grainy, aromatic pulp tasting of pineapple, guava, and mint all at once.

medlar.label: medlar
medlar.name: Medlar
medlar.description: A small brown fruit that must be softened by frost or extended storage, a process called bletting, before it becomes edible.

damson.label: damson
damson.name: Damson
damson.description: A small, tart wild plum with dark blue-black skin, most often cooked into jams and preserves rather than eaten fresh.

loquat.label: loquat
loquat.name: Loquat
loquat.description: A small orange fruit with downy skin and a sweet-tart flavor reminiscent of a mix between peach and citrus.

pawpaw.label: pawpaw
pawpaw.name: Pawpaw
pawpaw.description: North America's largest native fruit, with custardy yellow flesh tasting of banana and mango, though it bruises and spoils quickly.

tarragon.label: tarragon
tarragon.name: Tarragon
tarragon.description: A slender, anise-scented herb central to French cooking, most often infused into vinegar or butter rather than dried.

chervil.label: chervil
chervil.name: Chervil
chervil.description: A delicate, lacy-leaved herb with a mild flavor somewhere between parsley and anise, best added at the very end of cooking.

lovage.label: lovage
lovage.name: Lovage
lovage.description: A tall perennial herb whose leaves and stalks taste strongly of celery, used to season broths and soups.

hyssop.label: hyssop
hyssop.name: Hyssop
hyssop.description: An aromatic, minty herb with small blue flowers, historically used both as a flavoring and a strewing herb.

marjoram.label: marjoram
marjoram.name: Marjoram
marjoram.description: A sweet, milder cousin of oregano, with soft grey-green leaves used fresh at the end of cooking to preserve its delicate flavor.

savory.label: savory
savory.name: Savory
savory.description: A peppery herb available in a tender summer variety and a stronger, woodier winter variety, both used to season beans.

lemongrass.label: lemongrass
lemongrass.name: Lemongrass
lemongrass.description: A tall tropical grass whose fibrous stalks release a bright, citrusy oil when bruised or crushed, essential to many Southeast Asian broths.

catnip.label: catnip
catnip.name: Catnip
catnip.description: A minty herb whose nepetalactone oil triggers a euphoric response in most domestic cats, though it acts as a mild sedative on humans.

borage.label: borage
borage.name: Borage
borage.description: A fuzzy-leaved herb with star-shaped blue flowers and a cool, cucumber-like flavor, often floated in cold drinks.

rue.label: rue
rue.name: Rue
rue.description: A bitter, blue-green herb once widely used medicinally, though it is now used sparingly since it can irritate skin in sunlight.

angelica.label: angelica
angelica.name: Angelica
angelica.description: A tall, statuesque herb with hollow stems traditionally candied whole and used to decorate cakes and pastries.

sweet_cicely.label: sweet_cicely
sweet_cicely.name: Sweet cicely
sweet_cicely.description: A fern-leaved herb with a natural sweetness and mild anise flavor, sometimes used to cut the tartness of stewed fruit.

baobab.label: baobab
baobab.name: Baobab
baobab.description: An African tree with a massively swollen trunk that stores water through long dry seasons, earning it the nickname the tree of life.

banyan.label: banyan
banyan.name: Banyan
banyan.description: A fig species that grows aerial roots down from its branches, which thicken into new trunks so a single tree can spread over acres.

ginkgo.label: ginkgo
ginkgo.name: Ginkgo
ginkgo.description: An ancient tree species that has changed little in over 200 million years and is now valued mainly as a hardy, disease-resistant street tree.

dragon_blood_tree.label: dragon_blood_tree
dragon_blood_tree.name: Dragon blood tree
dragon_blood_tree.description: An umbrella-shaped tree native to a single remote archipelago, named for the dark red resin that seeps from any cut in its bark.

monkey_puzzle_tree.label: monkey_puzzle_tree
monkey_puzzle_tree.name: Monkey puzzle tree
monkey_puzzle_tree.description: A conifer covered in sharp, overlapping, scale-like leaves so dense and spiky that climbing it would puzzle even a monkey.

kapok.label: kapok
kapok.name: Kapok
kapok.description: A fast-growing tropical tree whose seed pods burst open to release a lightweight, water-resistant fiber once used to stuff life jackets.
kapok.comment: Seed fiber once stuffed life jackets

cedar_of_lebanon.label: cedar_of_lebanon
cedar_of_lebanon.name: Cedar of Lebanon
cedar_of_lebanon.description: A long-lived evergreen conifer with broad, flat-topped branches, historically prized as timber for ships and temples.

bristlecone_pine.label: bristlecone_pine
bristlecone_pine.name: Bristlecone pine
bristlecone_pine.description: A slow-growing high-altitude pine counted among the oldest living non-clonal organisms on Earth, with some individuals surpassing four thousand years old.

rainbow_eucalyptus.label: rainbow_eucalyptus
rainbow_eucalyptus.name: Rainbow eucalyptus
rainbow_eucalyptus.description: A fast-growing tree whose bark peels in patches to reveal streaks of green, orange, and purple underneath.

quaking_aspen.label: quaking_aspen
quaking_aspen.name: Quaking aspen
quaking_aspen.description: A tree whose flattened leaf stalks let each leaf flutter in the slightest breeze, and whose root systems can form single connected clonal colonies.
quaking_aspen.comment: Leaves flutter in the slightest breeze

japanese_maple.label: japanese_maple
japanese_maple.name: Japanese maple
japanese_maple.description: An ornamental maple prized for its finely lobed leaves that shift through vivid shades of red and orange in autumn.

cork_oak.label: cork_oak
cork_oak.name: Cork oak
cork_oak.description: An evergreen oak whose thick bark can be stripped for cork roughly once a decade without harming the tree.
cork_oak.comment: Bark harvested without harming the tree

protea.label: protea
protea.name: Protea
protea.description: A striking South African flower with a large central cone surrounded by stiff, colorful bracts, adapted to survive periodic wildfires.

corpse_flower.label: corpse_flower
corpse_flower.name: Corpse flower
corpse_flower.description: A rare flower that blooms for only a day or two roughly once a decade, releasing an odor of rotting flesh to attract carrion insects.

bird_of_paradise.label: bird_of_paradise
bird_of_paradise.name: Bird of paradise
bird_of_paradise.description: A tropical flower whose orange and blue petals emerge from a sheath in a shape resembling a bird's head and crest.

edelweiss.label: edelweiss
edelweiss.name: Edelweiss
edelweiss.description: A small, star-shaped alpine flower covered in fine white hairs that protect it from intense high-altitude sunlight and cold.

passionflower.label: passionflower
passionflower.name: Passionflower
passionflower.description: A climbing vine with an intricate, radial flower whose structure was once interpreted by missionaries as a symbol of the crucifixion.

black_bat_flower.label: black_bat_flower
black_bat_flower.name: Black bat flower
black_bat_flower.description: A shade-loving tropical flower with two dramatic wing-like bracts and long, whisker-like filaments trailing beneath it.

ghost_orchid.label: ghost_orchid
ghost_orchid.name: Ghost orchid
ghost_orchid.description: A leafless, chlorophyll-free orchid that appears to float on its host tree, pollinated by a single specialized moth species.

silversword.label: silversword
silversword.name: Silversword
silversword.description: A rosette-forming alpine plant found only on a few volcanic slopes, which flowers once after decades of growth and then dies.

lotus.label: lotus
lotus.name: Lotus
lotus.description: An aquatic flower whose waxy leaves and petals repel water and dirt completely, a self-cleaning effect studied for coatings and fabrics.

hibiscus.label: hibiscus
hibiscus.name: Hibiscus
hibiscus.description: A large, trumpet-shaped tropical flower whose petals are dried and steeped into a tart, deep red herbal tea.
hibiscus.comment: Petals steeped into tart red tea

foxglove.label: foxglove
foxglove.name: Foxglove
foxglove.description: A tall spike of tubular, spotted flowers that is the original source of a heart medication, though the whole plant is toxic if eaten.

larkspur.label: larkspur
larkspur.name: Larkspur
larkspur.description: A tall spire of delicate, spurred flowers in blues and purples, related to the buttercup and toxic to grazing livestock.

lions_mane_mushroom.label: lions_mane_mushroom
lions_mane_mushroom.name: Lion's mane mushroom
lions_mane_mushroom.description: A shaggy white mushroom made of long, icicle-like spines rather than gills, with a texture often compared to crab or lobster when cooked.

chanterelle.label: chanterelle
chanterelle.name: Chanterelle
chanterelle.description: A golden, trumpet-shaped wild mushroom with a fruity aroma often described as apricot-like, and shallow ridges rather than true gills.

morel.label: morel
morel.name: Morel
morel.description: A honeycomb-textured spring mushroom that must be cooked before eating, since it contains mild toxins that break down with heat.

puffball.label: puffball
puffball.name: Puffball
puffball.description: A round, sometimes basketball-sized fungus that releases a visible cloud of spores when its outer skin ruptures at maturity.
puffball.comment: Releases spores in a visible cloud

turkey_tail.label: turkey_tail
turkey_tail.name: Turkey tail
turkey_tail.description: A thin, fan-shaped bracket fungus banded in alternating colors that grows in overlapping tiers on dead hardwood logs.
turkey_tail.comment: Banded fan shape on dead wood

destroying_angel.label: destroying_angel
destroying_angel.name: Destroying angel
destroying_angel.description: An all-white, innocent-looking mushroom that is among the deadliest fungi known, responsible for many fatal misidentifications each year.

king_bolete.label: king_bolete
king_bolete.name: King bolete
king_bolete.description: A large, meaty wild mushroom with a spongy pore surface instead of gills, prized in European cooking as porcini.

shiitake.label: shiitake
shiitake.name: Shiitake
shiitake.description: A brown-capped mushroom traditionally cultivated on hardwood logs, valued for its savory, umami-rich flavor when cooked.

enoki.label: enoki
enoki.name: Enoki
enoki.description: A cultivated mushroom with long, thin white stems and tiny caps, grown crowded together in the dark to keep them pale and slender.
enoki.comment: Grown crowded together in the dark

ghost_fungus.label: ghost_fungus
ghost_fungus.name: Ghost fungus
ghost_fungus.description: A gilled fungus that glows a faint green in complete darkness, a phenomenon caused by a light-producing chemical reaction in its tissue.
ghost_fungus.comment: Glows faintly green in the dark

teff.label: teff
teff.name: Teff
teff.description: An extremely tiny East African grain, so small that a handful contains thousands of seeds, traditionally ground into flour for injera flatbread.

fonio.label: fonio
fonio.name: Fonio
fonio.description: A drought-tolerant West African grain that matures in as little as six to eight weeks, faster than almost any other cereal crop.
fonio.comment: Matures in as little as six weeks

spelt.label: spelt
spelt.name: Spelt
spelt.description: An ancient wheat relative with a tougher outer hull than modern wheat, which protects the grain but requires extra milling to remove.

amaranth.label: amaranth
amaranth.name: Amaranth
amaranth.description: A broadleaf plant grown for its tiny, protein-rich seeds, which pop slightly when toasted in a dry pan.

freekeh.label: freekeh
freekeh.name: Freekeh
freekeh.description: Young green wheat that is harvested early, then roasted over fire, which gives the grain a distinctive smoky flavor.
freekeh.comment: Green wheat roasted for smoky flavor

kamut.label: kamut
kamut.name: Kamut
kamut.description: An ancient variety of wheat with unusually large, golden kernels, marketed under its trademarked name khorasan.

farro.label: farro
farro.name: Farro
farro.description: A chewy, nutty ancient wheat grain that keeps its shape well when cooked, making it popular in grain salads.

jobs_tears.label: jobs_tears
jobs_tears.name: Job's tears
jobs_tears.description: A tall tropical grass grown for its hard, tear-shaped grains, which are used both as a food grain and strung into beads.
jobs_tears.comment: Grains are also strung into beads

sumac.label: sumac
sumac.name: Sumac
sumac.description: A tangy, brick-red spice ground from dried berries, used across the Middle East to add a lemony sourness without adding liquid.

asafoetida.label: asafoetida
asafoetida.name: Asafoetida
asafoetida.description: A pungent resin from a giant fennel-like plant that smells sharply of sulfur raw, but mellows into a savory, onion-like note when cooked in oil.

grains_of_paradise.label: grains_of_paradise
grains_of_paradise.name: Grains of paradise
grains_of_paradise.description: A peppery West African spice related to ginger, with a warm heat and a faint citrus and floral aroma.

long_pepper.label: long_pepper
long_pepper.name: Long pepper
long_pepper.description: An elongated, catkin-shaped relative of black pepper with a hotter, more complex heat, once more prized in Europe than pepper itself.

mahlab.label: mahlab
mahlab.name: Mahlab
mahlab.description: An aromatic spice ground from the pit inside a wild cherry species, with a flavor somewhere between almond and cherry, used in baking.

annatto.label: annatto
annatto.name: Annatto
annatto.description: Small, brick-red seeds from a tropical shrub, used more for the deep orange color they impart than for flavor.
annatto.comment: Used mainly for its orange color

galangal.label: galangal
galangal.name: Galangal
galangal.description: A rhizome related to ginger with a sharper, more citrusy and piney bite, essential to many Southeast Asian curry pastes.

fenugreek.label: fenugreek
fenugreek.name: Fenugreek
fenugreek.description: A small, angular seed with a bitter, maple-like aroma when toasted, widely used in South Asian spice blends.
fenugreek.comment: Bitter seed with a maple aroma

sichuan_pepper.label: sichuan_pepper
sichuan_pepper.name: Sichuan pepper
sichuan_pepper.description: A citrusy husk from a small shrub that produces a tingling, numbing sensation on the tongue rather than straightforward heat.

cubeb.label: cubeb
cubeb.name: Cubeb
cubeb.description: A relative of black pepper with a distinctive tail-like stem attached to each dried berry, giving it the nickname tailed pepper.

pangolin.label: pangolin
pangolin.name: Pangolin
pangolin.description: A scaly, ant-eating mammal that curls into a tight, armored ball when threatened. It is the most trafficked mammal in the world.

capybara.label: capybara
capybara.name: Capybara
capybara.description: The largest living rodent, a semi-aquatic South American mammal that lives in social groups near rivers and lakes.

okapi.label: okapi
okapi.name: Okapi
okapi.description: A forest-dwelling relative of the giraffe with zebra-striped legs, discovered by Western science only in the early twentieth century.
okapi.comment: A striped relative of the giraffe

quokka.label: quokka
quokka.name: Quokka
quokka.description: A small, stocky marsupial found mainly on a few Australian islands, known for an upturned mouth that gives it a permanent smile.

fossa.label: fossa
fossa.name: Fossa
fossa.description: Madagascar's largest carnivorous mammal, a slender, cat-like predator that hunts lemurs through the forest canopy.

saiga_antelope.label: saiga_antelope
saiga_antelope.name: Saiga antelope
saiga_antelope.description: A steppe-dwelling antelope with an unusually large, flexible nose thought to warm and filter the cold, dusty air it breathes.

aardvark.label: aardvark
aardvark.name: Aardvark
aardvark.description: A nocturnal, burrowing mammal with a long snout and sticky tongue, adapted almost entirely to feeding on ants and termites.

sloth.label: sloth
sloth.name: Sloth
sloth.description: A slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal whose fur hosts a small ecosystem of algae and insects, giving it a faint greenish tinge.
sloth.comment: Fur hosts its own tiny ecosystem

narwhal.label: narwhal
narwhal.name: Narwhal
narwhal.description: An Arctic whale whose males grow a single long, spiraled tusk, actually an elongated tooth, up to several meters long.

platypus.label: platypus
platypus.name: Platypus
platypus.description: An egg-laying mammal with a duck-like bill, webbed feet, and venomous spurs, combining traits so unusual it puzzled the scientists who first examined it.

tapir.label: tapir
tapir.name: Tapir
tapir.description: A pig-sized mammal with a short, flexible snout used like a small trunk to grasp leaves and fruit.
tapir.comment: Uses its snout like a small trunk

dhole.label: dhole
dhole.name: Dhole
dhole.description: A highly social Asian wild dog that hunts in large packs and communicates with an unusual range of whistles and calls.

binturong.label: binturong
binturong.name: Binturong
binturong.description: A shaggy, tree-dwelling mammal from Southeast Asian forests whose scent glands produce an odor often compared to buttered popcorn.

markhor.label: markhor
markhor.name: Markhor
markhor.description: A wild mountain goat known for its long, dramatically twisted, corkscrew-shaped horns.

gerenuk.label: gerenuk
gerenuk.name: Gerenuk
gerenuk.description: A long-necked African antelope that stands upright on its hind legs to browse leaves other grazers cannot reach.
gerenuk.comment: Stands on hind legs to browse

axolotl.label: axolotl
axolotl.name: Axolotl
axolotl.description: A Mexican salamander that typically never undergoes full metamorphosis, keeping its feathery external gills into adulthood, and can regrow entire lost limbs.

hellbender.label: hellbender
hellbender.name: Hellbender
hellbender.description: North America's largest salamander, a fully aquatic species that breathes partly through folds of loose skin along its sides.

olm.label: olm
olm.name: Olm
olm.description: A pale, blind cave salamander that can survive without food for years by slowing its metabolism to a near standstill.

poison_dart_frog.label: poison_dart_frog
poison_dart_frog.name: Poison dart frog
poison_dart_frog.description: A brightly colored rainforest frog whose vivid skin patterns warn predators of the potent toxins it secretes.
poison_dart_frog.comment: Bright colors warn of its toxins

caecilian.label: caecilian
caecilian.name: Caecilian
caecilian.description: A limbless, burrowing amphibian often mistaken for a large earthworm or snake, found in moist tropical soil.
caecilian.comment: Limbless and often mistaken for a worm

kakapo.label: kakapo
kakapo.name: Kakapo
kakapo.description: A large, flightless, nocturnal parrot from New Zealand that climbs trees and glides short distances instead of flying.

shoebill.label: shoebill
shoebill.name: Shoebill
shoebill.description: A tall African wading bird named for its massive, clog-shaped bill, which it uses to snatch fish and even small crocodiles.

harpy_eagle.label: harpy_eagle
harpy_eagle.name: Harpy eagle
harpy_eagle.description: One of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world, with talons roughly the size of a grizzly bear's claws.

secretarybird.label: secretarybird
secretarybird.name: Secretarybird
secretarybird.description: A long-legged African bird of prey that hunts on foot, stomping venomous snakes to death with powerful, rapid kicks.
secretarybird.comment: Stomps snakes to death on foot

resplendent_quetzal.label: resplendent_quetzal
resplendent_quetzal.name: Resplendent quetzal
resplendent_quetzal.description: A brilliantly iridescent Central American bird whose males trail elongated tail coverts once prized as a symbol of royalty.

hoatzin.label: hoatzin
hoatzin.name: Hoatzin
hoatzin.description: An Amazonian bird that ferments leaves in an enlarged crop much like a cow's rumen, giving it an earthy, musky odor.

kagu.label: kagu
kagu.name: Kagu
kagu.description: A ground-dwelling, nearly flightless bird found only in the forests of a single Pacific island, with a distinctive crest and bark-like call.

potoo.label: potoo
potoo.name: Potoo
potoo.description: A nocturnal bird that perches upright and motionless on broken branch stumps by day, camouflaged almost perfectly against detection.

lyrebird.label: lyrebird
lyrebird.name: Lyrebird
lyrebird.description: An Australian ground bird capable of mimicking an extraordinary range of sounds, from other birdsong to camera shutters and chainsaws.

cassowary.label: cassowary
cassowary.name: Cassowary
cassowary.description: A large, flightless rainforest bird with a bony head casque and a dagger-like inner claw, considered one of the most dangerous birds alive.

mudskipper.label: mudskipper
mudskipper.name: Mudskipper
mudskipper.description: An amphibious fish that spends much of its time out of water, breathing through its skin and moist gill chambers while skipping across mudflats.
mudskipper.comment: Spends most of its time out of water

anglerfish.label: anglerfish
anglerfish.name: Anglerfish
anglerfish.description: A deep-sea fish that dangles a glowing, bioluminescent lure above its mouth to attract prey in total darkness.
anglerfish.comment: Lures prey with a glowing appendage

lungfish.label: lungfish
lungfish.name: Lungfish
lungfish.description: An ancient fish lineage with a primitive lung that lets it survive out of water for months by burrowing into mud and going dormant.
lungfish.comment: Can survive buried in dried mud

arapaima.label: arapaima
arapaima.name: Arapaima
arapaima.description: One of the largest freshwater fish in the world, an Amazonian species that must surface periodically to gulp air.
arapaima.comment: Must surface periodically to breathe air

pufferfish.label: pufferfish
pufferfish.name: Pufferfish
pufferfish.description: A fish that inflates its body into a spiny ball when threatened and carries a potent neurotoxin in its skin and organs.

flying_fish.label: flying_fish
flying_fish.name: Flying fish
flying_fish.description: A fish with oversized, wing-like pectoral fins that let it glide well above the water's surface to escape underwater predators.
flying_fish.comment: Glides above the water on winglike fins

seahorse.label: seahorse
seahorse.name: Seahorse
seahorse.description: A small, upright-swimming fish notable because it is the male that carries the fertilized eggs in a specialized brood pouch.

lamprey.label: lamprey
lamprey.name: Lamprey
lamprey.description: A primitive, jawless fish with a circular, tooth-lined mouth used to latch onto other fish and feed on their blood and tissue.

atlas_moth.label: atlas_moth
atlas_moth.name: Atlas moth
atlas_moth.description: One of the largest moths in the world by wing surface area, with wingtips patterned to resemble a snake's head to deter predators.

goliath_beetle.label: goliath_beetle
goliath_beetle.name: Goliath beetle
goliath_beetle.description: Among the heaviest insects on Earth, an African beetle whose larvae can outweigh a small mammal before pupating.

luna_moth.label: luna_moth
luna_moth.name: Luna moth
luna_moth.description: A pale green moth with long, trailing hindwing tails and no functional mouthparts, since its short adult life is spent only reproducing.

bombardier_beetle.label: bombardier_beetle
bombardier_beetle.name: Bombardier beetle
bombardier_beetle.description: A beetle that defends itself by mixing chemicals in an internal chamber to spray a boiling, noxious jet at attackers.

leafcutter_ant.label: leafcutter_ant
leafcutter_ant.name: Leafcutter ant
leafcutter_ant.description: A highly social ant that slices leaf fragments to carry back to the colony, not to eat directly but to cultivate a fungus garden.
leafcutter_ant.comment: Farms fungus instead of eating leaves

praying_mantis.label: praying_mantis
praying_mantis.name: Praying mantis
praying_mantis.description: An ambush predator insect with forelegs folded as if in prayer, and specialized joints that let it turn its head nearly all the way around.
praying_mantis.comment: Can turn its head almost fully around

monarch_butterfly.label: monarch_butterfly
monarch_butterfly.name: Monarch butterfly
monarch_butterfly.description: A butterfly famous for a multigenerational migration spanning thousands of miles, with no single individual completing the full round trip.
monarch_butterfly.comment: No single butterfly completes the migration

dung_beetle.label: dung_beetle
dung_beetle.name: Dung beetle
dung_beetle.description: An insect that rolls and buries animal dung both as a food source and a brood chamber, and some species navigate by the stars.
dung_beetle.comment: Some species navigate using the stars

firefly.label: firefly
firefly.name: Firefly
firefly.description: A beetle that produces cold, chemical light from its abdomen in flashing patterns used to attract mates of the same species.
firefly.comment: Produces cold light from its abdomen

cicada.label: cicada
cicada.name: Cicada
cicada.description: An insect known for loud mating calls and, in some species, a life cycle of thirteen or seventeen years spent almost entirely underground.

komodo_dragon.label: komodo_dragon
komodo_dragon.name: Komodo dragon
komodo_dragon.description: The largest living lizard species, an Indonesian monitor lizard with a mildly venomous bite that weakens large prey over time.

tuatara.label: tuatara
tuatara.name: Tuatara
tuatara.description: A reptile found only in New Zealand that looks lizard-like but belongs to an ancient lineage otherwise extinct for over a hundred million years.
tuatara.comment: Last survivor of an ancient lineage

thorny_devil.label: thorny_devil
thorny_devil.name: Thorny devil
thorny_devil.description: An Australian desert lizard covered entirely in defensive spines, which also channel dew and rainwater along grooves directly to its mouth.
thorny_devil.comment: Spines also channel water to its mouth

gila_monster.label: gila_monster
gila_monster.name: Gila monster
gila_monster.description: One of the few venomous lizard species, a slow-moving desert reptile that delivers venom by chewing rather than injecting through fangs.

veiled_chameleon.label: veiled_chameleon
veiled_chameleon.name: Veiled chameleon
veiled_chameleon.description: A tree-dwelling lizard with a tall casque on its head and eyes that swivel independently to watch two directions at once.
veiled_chameleon.comment: Eyes swivel independently of each other

gharial.label: gharial
gharial.name: Gharial
gharial.description: A fish-eating crocodilian with an extremely narrow, elongated snout adapted for quick sideways snapping through water.

matamata_turtle.label: matamata_turtle
matamata_turtle.name: Matamata turtle
matamata_turtle.description: A South American freshwater turtle with a bark-textured shell and a flattened, leaf-like head that camouflages it while it ambushes fish.

flying_gecko.label: flying_gecko
flying_gecko.name: Flying gecko
flying_gecko.description: A gecko with folds of skin along its body and tail that spread out to let it glide between trees rather than fall.

malachite.label: malachite
malachite.name: Malachite
malachite.description: A vivid green banded mineral that forms from copper deposits, historically ground into pigment and jewelry.

azurite.label: azurite
azurite.name: Azurite
azurite.description: A deep blue copper mineral that often forms alongside malachite and slowly weathers into it over geological time.

moonstone.label: moonstone
moonstone.name: Moonstone
moonstone.description: A feldspar mineral prized for an internal glow called adularescence, caused by light scattering between microscopic internal layers.

obsidian.label: obsidian
obsidian.name: Obsidian
obsidian.description: A naturally occurring volcanic glass formed when lava cools too quickly for crystals to form, fracturing into edges sharp enough for ancient blades.
obsidian.comment: Volcanic glass sharp enough for blades

pyrite.label: pyrite
pyrite.name: Pyrite
pyrite.description: A brassy, metallic mineral nicknamed fool's gold for its resemblance to real gold, though it is far more brittle and common.

opal.label: opal
opal.name: Opal
opal.description: A mineraloid made of tiny silica spheres that diffract light into shifting flashes of color known as play-of-color.

labradorite.label: labradorite
labradorite.name: Labradorite
labradorite.description: A feldspar mineral that flashes bright blues and greens, an optical effect called labradorescence caused by internal layering.

tourmaline.label: tourmaline
tourmaline.name: Tourmaline
tourmaline.description: A crystal family that occurs in nearly every color, sometimes within a single crystal, and can even generate a static charge when heated.

selenite.label: selenite
selenite.name: Selenite
selenite.description: A soft, translucent form of gypsum that grows in long, flexible crystal blades and can sometimes be scratched with a fingernail.
selenite.comment: Soft enough to scratch with a nail

lapis_lazuli.label: lapis_lazuli
lapis_lazuli.name: Lapis lazuli
lapis_lazuli.description: A deep blue metamorphic rock flecked with golden pyrite, historically ground into the pigment ultramarine.
